list: **Holton, D., Mackridge, P. & Philippaki-Warburton, I.** *Greek: An Essential Grammar of the Modern Language*, 2nd edition. London: Routledge, 2016. The main reference, already extracted into the app's grammar data (data/grammar/): noun and adjective declension (ch. 3), pronouns (ch. 4), numerals (ch. 5), the verb (ch. 6, including the table of irregular verbs in §6.25), adverbs (ch. 7), prepositions (ch. 8), conjunctions (ch. 9), the sentence and its clauses (ch. 10), word formation (ch. 11) and conversational features (ch. 12). Copyrighted: no text is reproduced; rules are restated and all examples are new. Chapters 38–44 add the topics from chapters 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12 and Appendix 2 that the first edition of this outline left out.

**Πουλοπούλου, Σ. (Poulopoulou, S.)** *Modern Greek: Grammar Notes for Absolute Beginners (A1–A2).* Athens: Σύνδεσμος Ελληνικών Ακαδημαϊκών Βιβλιοθηκών / Kallipos, 2015. Licensed **CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 GR**. Used for the present-tense verb groups (ch. 4 of the notes), the noun phrase and its dependents (ch. 5), pronouns (ch. 6), the aorist (ch. 8), the future and the dependent forms (ch. 9) and the appendix of verbs. Following the licence: credited here, used non-commercially, and derived material shared under the same terms.

**Πύλη για την ελληνική γλώσσα** (greek-language.gr, Κέντρο Ελληνικής Γλώσσας), with the *Λεξικό της Κοινής Νεοελληνικής* (Ινστιτούτο Νεοελληνικών Σπουδών, Ίδρυμα Μανόλη Τριανταφυλλίδη, 1998). The app's lexicon, used here to check words and forms, was audited against it on 25 October 2026.
**Κέντρο Ελληνικής Γλώσσας.** Πιστοποίηση Επάρκειας της Ελληνομάθειας (Certificate of Attainment in Greek), level descriptions A1–C2. Used to grade each section A1–C1.
**Wiktionary (en.wiktionary.org)**, through the **kaikki.org** extract, as used by the app's declension and conjugation drill books.
**LibreOffice el_GR spelling dictionary** (github.com/LibreOffice/dictionaries). Every Greek word in the outline was run through it.
**This app's own data**: the 8,214-entry annotated lexicon with its forms index, the drill books, the syntax guide and the grammar cards. The "Go deeper" links lead into them.
**Holton, D., Mackridge, P., Philippaki-Warburton, I. & Spyropoulos, V.** *Greek: A Comprehensive Grammar*, 2nd edition. London: Routledge, 2012. The larger companion to the Essential Grammar.
**Ίδρυμα Μανόλη Τριανταφυλλίδη.** *Νεοελληνική Γραμματική (της Δημοτικής)*, 1941, reprinted by the Institute in Thessaloniki. The classic school grammar of Demotic.
**Κλαίρης, Χ. & Μπαμπινιώτης, Γ.** *Γραμματική της Νέας Ελληνικής: Δομολειτουργική – Επικοινωνιακή.* Athens: Ελληνικά Γράμματα, 2005.
**Mackridge, P.** *The Modern Greek Language: A Descriptive Analysis of Standard Modern Greek.* Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1985.
**Μπαμπινιώτης, Γ.** *Λεξικό της Νέας Ελληνικής Γλώσσας*, 4th edition. Athens: Κέντρο Λεξικολογίας, 2012.

body.p: 1. **Rules** were written to agree with Holton et al. (2016) and Poulopoulou (2015). Where colloquial and standard usage differ (όταν θα έρθεις / όταν έρθεις, μίλαγα / μιλούσα, ήμουνα, θες, είπανε), the text says which is which. 2. **Verb forms against Holton**: tools/theoria/crosscheck.py compares the outline's verb tables with Holton's table of irregular verbs (§6.25). 37 aorist, passive aorist and participle forms were compared, with no differences. 3. **Drills**: every multiple-choice item has exactly one correct option; the build refuses an item with no answer, two answers, duplicate options or a missing explanation. Wrong options were reviewed so that none is a correct alternative (a valid colloquial form, a formal variant, or a different but acceptable tense). 4. **Typed answers** accept the common correct variants (ακόμα / ακόμη, word order, colloquial endings, both spellings where the dictionaries allow two), and a missing accent or final -ν counts as "almost right" rather than wrong. 5. **Word-order tiles** only accept alternative orders made of the same words. 6. **Spelling and accents**: tools/theoria/check.js runs all Greek text through the el_GR dictionary and checks one accent per word (except before enclitics), the final-ν rule for την / στην / δεν / μην, and mixed Latin and Greek letters. Three final-ν slips and one wrong aorist (μοιάζω → έμοιασα) were found this way and corrected. Remaining flags are deliberate: wrong forms quoted inside explanations, stems and endings shown on their own, unaccented words in the stress-mark exercises, and μη before adjectives (μη πραγματικός), which never takes ν. 7. **Lint**: tools/theoria/lint.py rejects drafting slips, English left inside Greek options and distractors padded with extra words. 8. **Links**: every "Go deeper" link to a lesson, guide, card or drill book is resolved at build time; a broken link stops the build.

9. **Part Η΄ (chapters 38–47, added 5 November 2026)** came from a gap check: every section heading of Holton et al. (2016) and the B2 descriptors of the Κέντρο Ελληνικής Γλώσσας were matched against what the app already taught, and the uncovered topics were written up. They rest on Holton ch. 5 (§5.5 numerals in use), ch. 6 (§6.1 the verb phrase: objects, double accusative, the ethic genitive, linking verbs), ch. 9 (§9.1 coordinating conjunctions, §9.3.6–9.3.7 deictic να and hortatory για), ch. 10 (§10.3–10.4 suggestions and prohibitions, §10.8 exclamations, §10.16 manner, §10.21 coordination, §10.22 comparison and equation), ch. 11 and Appendix 2 (abbreviations), and ch. 12 (§12.1–12.3 politeness, names and wishes); the spelling and punctuation chapter follows the Τριανταφυλλίδης grammar and the monotonic conventions of the *Λεξικό της Κοινής Νεοελληνικής*. The same check found one error in the existing text: three and four and a half split by gender (**τρεισήμισι** for masculine and feminine nouns, **τριάμισι** for neuter ones; likewise **τεσσερισήμισι / τεσσεράμισι**). Chapter 14 and the numeral guide (#pos) had treated τρεισήμισι as unchangeable; both now give the split.

Chapter 47 adds the learned syntax of C1 reading texts (learned prepositions, ως, formal conjunctions, frozen forms). Chapter 46 drills aspect as minimal pairs across every tense. Chapter 45 mixes the whole outline in the task types of the B2 language section (word formation, one-word gaps, transformations, choosing the form, error correction); many of its items use words added to the lexicon on 5 November 2026 (data/lexicon/build/added-10k.json).

The figures at the time of writing: 47 chapters in eight parts, 280 sections, 842 solved problems and 3,159 drills (1,647 multiple choice, 1,255 typed answers, 257 word-order), all in spaced review. A graded review path (25 stages: groups of up to three chapters in book order, a checkpoint at the end of each part, a final review) mixes each stage's drills with earlier chapters and opens the next stage at 80%.

body.tip: Found a mistake? The source files are in library/theoria/src/ and rebuild with python3 library/theoria/src/build.py.

title: References and validation
blurb: The grammars and dictionaries this outline was checked against, what each chapter rests on, and how the content and the drills were validated.

intro.p: This outline restates the grammar of Standard Modern Greek in its own words, with its own everyday examples. Its rules follow the reference grammars below; its Greek was run through a spelling dictionary, and its drills through the build, lint and cross-check tools described at the end. It is a personal, non-commercial study resource.
